PC: Obtain intravenous (IV) access, place on monitor, apply oxygen, and obtain vital signs
Promptly perform focused History and Physical Exam
Discover complaints of dyspnea, itching rash, and facial swelling
Identify tachycardia, wheezing, and urticaria on exam
Recognize anaphylaxis and treat with appropriate dose/route of epinephrine
Collect adjuncts and difficult airway equipment (eg NPA, OPA, stylet, bougie, scalpel/cric kit)
Attempt to pre-oxygenate with non-rebreather at high flow rate
Assemble equipment, at minimum: Bag-valve-mask (BVM) attached to O2, suction, laryngoscope (confirmed functional), endotracheal tube (size 7.0-8.0, confirmed intact balloon), stethoscope
Recognize and utilize an acceptable sedative at correct dose for RSI:E.g. Etomidate, 0.2-0.4mg/kg IV, Ketamine, 1-2mg/kg IV, or Propofol 1-3mg/kg IV

Perform endotracheal intubation, and verbalize confirmation with multiple methods (e.g. direct visualization, fog in tube, absent epigastric sounds, bilateral chest rise, bilateral breath sounds) that must include end-tidal CO2 colorimetry or capnography
Do not release ETT until securely fixed with tape or securement device
Ensure patient secured with non-violent restraints after procedure
MK: Verbalize impending breathing failure despite maximal non-invasive methods
SBP: Recruit multiple healthcare workers to assist
Recognize need for backups for possible difficult intubation
Promptly admit to medical intensive care unit (ICU) after patient is stabilized
ICS: Promptly lead team in successful intubation
Update family once initial stabilization complete
Discuss presentation, evaluation, current diagnosis, severity and next steps
